spans.s: R2k गणस् and four-fold ब्राह्- मणस्. वा. ६१. ६७; ९९. २५४.

(I)--Indra's thunderbolt; a weapon shaped out of दधीचि's limbs by विश्वकर्मन् for the use of Indra; with this Indra was able to break the back of the mountains. By this वृत्र was slain. But it was of no use against Namuci; the embodiment of Brahmanical energy;
1: भा. VI. १०. १३; VIII. ११. ३३-36;

(II)--a son of Aniruddha and सुभद्रा, and father of प्रतिबाहु: Installed king of शूरसेनस् at मथुरा by युधिष्ठिर after Arjuna crowned him at Indraprastha after the decease of कृष्ण. भा. X. ९०. ३७-38; I. १५. ३९; XI. ३१. २५; Vi. IV. १५. ४१-2; V. ३२. 6; ३७. ६३-65.

(III)--a thief of काञ्ची stole bit by bit from the city and stored the riches in a secret place in the neighbour- ing woods. A certain किरात gathering fuel for sale observed this once and took a portion of the property home. His wife, charitably disposed, wanted to utilise it for digging [page३-137+ २९] wells and ponds. So a pond was constructed but before it was completed, all money had been spent. He got more of the thief's wealth and completed the embankment; built temples of शिव and विष्णु, besides giving gifts to ब्राह्मणस् who were pleased and renamed him and his wife as Dvijavarma and शीलावती: He also built a town and named it after his Purohita, देवरात. At his death, as he built all out of stolen wealth नारद ruled that he should wander in air for १२ years, while his wife went to Brahmaloka. As she refused, she was advised to recite शतरुद्र and get her husband released from the sin of theft. When Vajra died he got half of Dvijavarman's virtue. Dvijavarman attained कैलास. Br.
(V)--a son of अश्वसुत and Sutanu. वा. ९६. २५१; १०९. 3.
(II)--a R. sacred to ललिता. Br. IV. ३३. २९-33.
--शाल्मलि--one of the twenty-eight hells. Here the punishment is by piercing one with शाल्मलि thorns for beastliness. भा. V. २६. 7 and २१.
--the place where the राक्षसस् named नीलकस् live. वा. ३९. ३०.
--a boundary hill in प्लक्षद्वीप. भा. V. २०. 4. [page३-138+ २७]
(I)--the name of the lion on which ललिता rode to meet भण्ड. Br. IV. १७. 9.
(II)--a son, and a commander of भण्ड. Br. IV. २१. ८१; २६. ४७.
--a commander of भण्ड, who was killed by the शक्तिस्. Br. IV. २१. ७७; २३. ४६-9.

--an Asura who took part in the देवा- sura war between Bali and Indra;
1: भा. VIII. १०. २०.
helped in the churning of the ocean.
2: M. २४९. ६७.
(I)--a son of Balasthala; was made of a portion of the sun. His son was Khagana. भा. IX. १
(II)--a son of उलूक, (Utka-वि। प्।) and father of शङ्खन. Br. III. ६३. २०५; Vi.

(I)--a son of घोष(vasu) and father of भागवत;
1: भा.

. १७-18; Vi. IV. २४. ३५.
a शुन्ग ruler, ruled for seven years.
2: Br. III. ७४. १५४.
[page३-139+ २७]
--a powerful son of Ugra, the राक्षस. Br.

--a son of Diti after her penance and father of Asura तारक who gave trouble to the devas; while a boy, under the orders of his mother, had Indra bound and placed before Diti; ब्रह्मा and कश्यप medi- ated and set him free; ब्रह्मा gave him for wife a mind- born daughter, वराङ्गी, with whom he went to penance; when वराङ्गी was engaged in तपस् Indra threatened her with several guises of the monkey, serpent, jackal, etc., which made her weep in sorrow and fear; meanwhile Vaj- राङ्ग's penance had ended and ब्रह्मा had blessed him. He came in search of his wife whom he found crying in fear. [page३-140+ ३३] She spoke of the insult offered by Indra and asked for a son, तारक, able to vanquish Indra. Then again he entered into a terrible vow when ब्रह्मा blessed him with the son desired by his spouse. तारक was born and great festivities were held in his honour. Soon he was crowned king of the Asura world. M. १४६. 5, ४१ ff; १४
--a son of उपासन्ग (उपान्ग-वा। प्।). Br. III. ७१. २५८; वा. ९६. २४९.
--one of the ten पीठस् for images; with 3 to 6 मेखलस्; this gives one long life. M. २६२. 7, १०, १८.
--the ब्राह्मणस् established by Jana- mejaya. वा. ९९. २५०.
--the यजुस् शाखस् imparted by the Sun god to याज्ञवल्क्य. These were fifteen branches each com- prising hundreds of यजुस् (sentences). These were learnt by कण्व, माध्यन्दिन and others. भा.
--a son of Arka Agni. Br. II. १२. ४३.
--one of the ten horses yoked to the chariot of the Moon. Br. II. २३. ५६.
--a horse of the Moon's chariot. M. १२६. ५२. [page३-185+ २५]

--the common name to the fifteen pupils of याज्ञवल्क्य;
1: Br. II. ३५. २६, ३०; वा. ६१. २४-6; Vi.

. ७६.
the Yajus granted to याज्- ञवल्क्य as horse by सूर्य.
3: वा. ६१. २२.
--the sons of भद्रा; of different colours and able to fly in the air; white, pink, red, black, green and grey for use by the devas. वा. ६६. ७३-4.
--the incarnation of हयग्रीव who restored the Angas, Vedas, पुराणस्, धर्मशास्त्रस्, न्याय and मीमाम्स when all the universe was burnt. M. ५३. 5.
